item.title: @GaryMarcus：人工智能长期通过树搜索方法解决复杂高维搜索空间问题
item.description:
reality: people have been brute forcing important AI solutions with tree search since before LLMs were born. DeepBlue, for example, in 1997.

Sad that most people have no idea about the history of AI.

Footnote: part of the reason that LLMs work better nowadays is because they finally learned to borrow tree search from classical symbolic AI.

@Kekius_Sage：AI can brute-force through high-dimensional search spaces faster than we can blink. First was Navier Stokes, now is Riemann hypothesis.

Still, only a human brain can define the idea that changes how the next generation thinks.

Human value does not shrink when AI gets smarter. We just move from being the calculators to being the meaning-makers.

@ChombaBupe：The universal approximation theorem states, any neural network (NN) with at least one hidden layer & enough nonlinear activation nodes in the hidden layers, can approximate any function but it doesn't say that that NN can learn any function given input-output pairs.

item.title: @GaryMarcus：分析软银资产结构与负债比例在AI市场波动下面临的风险
item.description:
oh well. i tried to warn Masa that this might not work out

@ddkun_：ソフトバンク崩壊のシナリオが近づいてきている。ソフトバンクの資産は、現状ほとんどがArm(18.6兆円、86%保有)とOpenAI(16兆円、13%保有)のわずか2社。どちらも実際には市場で売ることができない資産だ。
一方で、純有利子負債は11.3兆円。これだけ見ると余裕に見えるが、先述の通り資産のほとんどは売れない株に依存している。
ソフトバンク自身も、資産に対する負債の割合=LTVを25%以内に収めると説明し、銀行や債権者もそれを信用して貸付を行なっている。9月30日時点でのLTVは15.9%だった。
しかし、Anthropicの上場とその後の株価急落によって状況は一変した。Anthropicでさえ時価総額が1.2兆ドルしかつかない状況では、OpenAIにはそれ以下の株価しかつかない。IPO自体が頓挫する可能性すらある。
OpenAIのIPOが頓挫する時には、同時にAI株全体が暴落するときでもある。Armも当然大きく下落するだろう。
すでに、足元のArm株の下落によってLTVは25%を超えていると思われる。ソフトバンクが債権者に約束している数字を超えてしまった。
ここからさらにOpenAIへの投資の16兆円の投資が回収不能になると、もはやソフトバンクの財務は再起不能になってしまう。ソフトバンクほどの大企業が吹き飛ぶ時は、日本経済への影響も甚大なものになるだろう。

item.title: @firstadopter：评论认为Anthropic的IPO股份分配策略对长期投资者不够优化
item.description:
This Anthropic IPO allocation strategy was suboptimal and myopic. I heard from many long-only firms that received zero shares and they were VERY annoyed.

You want to spread the allocation as much as possible across long-term oriented firms that invest on multi-year time frames.

Giving them a starter position makes them much more likely to buy more in the aftermarket, rather than ticking them off.

Allocating more shares to hedge funds or rewarding friendly early VC firms that are more likely flip and already have massive exposure is not the best approach.

Anthropic needs to think about building allies in the next chapter, not the past.

@firstadopter：They should have allocated more shares to long-term oriented long-only investors. That's basic IPO strategy stuff.

WSJ: "Some investors question how the company and its bankers doled out the $81 billion worth of shares in the IPO. More than half went to investors who already had stakes in the company, including Altimeter Capital, Lightspeed Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures, according to people familiar with the matter, an unusually high portion reflecting Anthropic executives’ desire to reward early backers.

Some of those early backers were venture-capital firms, which were prevented from selling their pre-existing stakes. Those firms don’t typically get big allotments in IPO shares, which they would be free to sell immediately to lock in gains."

"Anthropic also allocated significant portions of IPO shares to big investment firms such as Citadel" https://www.wsj.com/finance/stocks/the-blame-game-has-begun-over-anthropics-turbulent-trading-debut-280a34b1?mod=hp_lead_pos1

item.title: @GaryMarcus：学者探讨黎曼猜想证明中的方法论细节，指出系统并非纯粹依靠大语言模型单次提示直接得出答案
item.description:
why the methods in the Riemann result matter, and why most people are probably misenvisioning what happened.

@GaryMarcus：As noted elsewhere I would really like to know what the methodology was, but e.g. one report sggests that agentic loops in which bits of proof were fed through lean and then iterated on, in which case lean was an essential part of the cognitive system that did the proof.

so too was Alpoge, who also add his mathematical judgement

so it’s not like a pure LLM came out with the answer from a prompt “solve riemann” in the way that some people are erroneously envisioning.

of course i doubt that Claude is a pure LLM at this point; we know for a fact that Claude code is a neurosymbolic hybrid (what I long favored) and i imagine Claude is.

item.title: @convequity：MicroVision拥有光连接插件模块，其时间表及市场适应性仍存不确定性
item.description:
$MVIS has one concrete optical-connectivity product: a pluggable module holding an external laser, built on the same photonic chip as its Scantinel FMCW LiDAR.

Its Scantinel subsidiary introduced it in September 2026 for co-packaged optics, targeting scale-up networks inside AI data centres. The company says the light source can be serviced separately from the chip package it feeds.

MicroVision also paid $33 million for assets of Luminar's LiDAR sensor business, an acquisition that closed in February 2026.

MicroVision said it was in discussions with potential licensees and development partners, an earlier stage than $AEVA's signed development agreement.

Its two LiDAR technologies use different sensing methods and components, so each would need separate work to meet optical-networking requirements. Our working concern is that MicroVision may need more adaptation and qualification than Aeva, so its time to market is less certain.

Deeper dive available at Convequity.
